records.subject: Dual-cell electrochemical heat engine
records.object: Conversion efficiency approaching the Carnot limit
records.quote: Our theoretical analysis revealed for the first time that in the dual-cell electrochemical system, the flow rate must be controlled as a response to the electrical current, and conversion efficiency no longer depend on the conventional ther-moelectric figure-of-merit.
context_quotes: Based on established principles and considering tremendous advancements for the past 10 years within thermogalavic materials and flow battery systems, our analysis presents that it is realistic to develop dual-cell electrochemical heat engines that can be operated at conversion efficiencies approaching the Carnot limit, reaching 10.1 % and 19.3 % at maximum power point and maximum conversion efficiency con-ditions, respectively, under the temperature gradient of 80 degrees C.
modality_evidence: Our theoretical analysis revealed for the first time that in the dual-cell electrochemical system, the flow rate must be controlled as a response to the electrical current, and conversion efficiency no longer depend on the conventional ther-moelectric figure-of-merit.
records.conditions: Analysis based on established principles and advances in thermogalvanic materials and flow batteries; temperature gradient of 80 °C.
